parsed.explanation: The combined regime presents tier-1/2 universal exposures: federal entry officers are instructed to refuse visa cases where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and to consider lifetime fraud findings, passports must match birth-assigned sex, and X markers are terminated — so every trans visitor passes through a sex-scrutinising border. Facility bans across many units plus a documented trespass arrest (24h in men's ward) create criminal exposure in government buildings; this unit has no GI nondiscrimination law, a surgical-only birth-certificate rule, reverted licence policy, Medicaid bar for all ages, and care-ban liability pushing providers to refuse visitors' refills. Mitigations are partial: GI hate-crime coverage, sanctuary cities, working courts that sometimes block orders — but the highest state court recently affirmed the care ban, and national courts are mixed. Consequences on outing run from humiliation and ejection to short custody; imprisonment is possible but not typical. This sits just below anchor 0.45-C/0.45-D territory and clearly below 0.55.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: passport must show birth-assigned sex, X markers stopped, visa cable instructs refusal on 'reasonable doubt' about sex and possible permanent fraud finding; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding; allied governments issued trans-specific advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, waivers exist, litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document mismatch at entry can cascade into fraud allegation, secondary inspection, detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national-level: detained trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; corrections bureau adopts conversion-therapy-style policies and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for visitor detention specifically.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa refusal or document doubt can route a visitor into this custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans per gender identity across ~21+ units; in 4 units criminal exposure; documented arrest of a trans woman in a women's restroom, handcuffed, 24h held in men's ward; this unit's trespass offence covers public buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; exemptions exist; most units have no ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airport, capitol, and government-building use creates arrest exposure; ward placement by birth sex documented.

care_services.exposure: SAFE Act: minor care banned (upheld by highest court 2026), Medicaid bar all ages, provider licence loss and 15-year suits chill adult care; HB 2009 cuts custody care with no taper; minors travelling with a guardian cannot obtain care here.
care_services.protection: Two sanctuary cities; emergency care not specifically restricted.
care_services.interaction: Visitors losing medication mid-trip face refusals; travelling family cannot access youth care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame care as 'mutilation', directive to prosecute teachers facilitating transition, counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups, state tipline invites anonymous reporting of 'gender transition intervention'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Some orders enjoined; statement that disagreement alone is not targeted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises discovery stakes and licenses private and official hostility toward visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces total ban on initiating care, already-upheld ban; guardians of trans youth in a hostile regime; schools-EO targets facilitation though aimed at residents.
minors_guardians.protection: Those already in treatment may continue under SAFE Act (residents); sanctuary cities.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian seeking care for a minor engages provider criminal/licence exposure and state tipline.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated trans-specific violence incident in this unit documented; national hate-crime data show sexual-orientation bias incidents; police hostility documented mainly via restroom arrest.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Enforcement of facility law, not street violence, is the documented police exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Recourse uneven: no GI nondiscrimination law; oversight/courts often uphold hostile statutes (highest court affirmed ban); complaints mechanisms limited; 2026 legislative trajectory toward permanence.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working courts have enjoined some national orders; litigation ongoing; sanctuary-city ordinances operative.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court outcomes diverge across units, making exposure unpredictable at time of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: pervasive identity-verification gatekeeping (entry cable, document rules) with private and official scrutiny throughout daily life; custodial prosecution uncommon. This jurisdiction adds documented custody abuses and a facility arrest, sitting slightly below 0.45-C.

0.45-D's registration database durably exposes visitors; here the sex-based passport/visa regime and tipline create comparable universal discovery exposure, plus documented custody harm — comparable or marginally worse than 0.45-D.

0.55-A's worst outcome is overnight holding without charge; here the same friction tier exists but compounded by care denial for minors, custody-abuse record, and criminalised facility use in-unit — materially below 0.55-A.

0.25-C features birth-sex prison placement with frequent assaults and cross-dressing arrests; this jurisdiction's custody harms are documented but largely in immigration/national custody, and visitor imprisonment is not typical — clearly above 0.25-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime chains federal sex-scrutiny at entry (birth-sex passports, refusal-and-fraud instructions) into in-country exposure: facility bans with criminal trespass in some units, no state GI nondiscrimination, surgical-only marker rules, and a care landscape where a travelling minor is fully barred and an adult's refills are chilled by provider liability. Documented custody harms (immigration detention abuse, corrections care cuts) await anyone routed from document doubt into detention. Partial mitigations — hate-crime coverage, sanctuary cities, active litigation and occasional injunctions — soften but do not neutralise tier-1/2 universal exposures, and the state's highest court recently entrenched the care ban. Net: Elevated Risk, low 0.40s.
